findings:
The re-plan fixes all 14 problems from the first review. The test-time budget is now added up correctly and covers both exit measurements. The Laser Tender has moved to a window that stays under the frozen enemy-density limit. The turret group sits clear of level 1's laser columns, and a test checks that. The tasks that share files now run one after another. The arithmetic was recomputed from the code and holds. The review found six small issues. Each can be fixed inside the task that owns it, and none changes the design, so I approve. One caveat: the implementing agents only see their plan sections, not this review. Before releasing the tasks, please copy fixes M1 and M4 into the plan, or into the descriptions of t12, t14 and t6. They are the two that could turn a test red or confuse a build.

| # | Severity | Problem | Fix | Tasks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | minor | The twin drones' exit probe runs at one speed (1083 runs, against the 2166 budgeted), and the drone's "exit along −n" rule has no `n` in the probe's lone-drone start, so the run either never moves or measures a rule the drone does not use. | Give the drone's DISENGAGE the shared nearest-edge exit (or define its heading without a rig), pass `[max carry-in speed, 10.0]` as Phases 5 and 7 do, and record the choice in DECISIONS. | t12, t14 |
| M2 | minor | The real-frame beam-cadence row can be blurred by the player's shield charges, which absorb a hit without a health change, so it passes with 3 hits instead of 4. | Count damage events (health drops plus charges consumed), or zero the charges first. | t2 |
| M3 | minor | The "hub frame-time note" is listed as a GUT row, but 2 × 600 real hub frames would cost far more than t18's 1.2 s allotment. | Measure it once outside GUT and record it in DECISIONS, as Phase 7 did. | t18 |
| M4 | minor | t6 depends only on t1, yet its section describes `power_down()` and COMMIT-light branches for beams and rings that t2 and t3 create. | Build only the burst-cannon branch in t6 and leave the beam and ring branches to t7 and t8, or add t2 to t6's `dependsOn`. | t6 |
| M5 | minor | The fire-lane coverage rule counts mounts, so the hub site's heavy emplacement, with two mounts, satisfies it alone, and the rule cannot reject a site that has one shooter. | Count mounts on at least 2 different hosts, and keep the turret-removed boundary. | t9, t18 |
| M6 | minor | t10 is sized medium but carries a new `BaseEnemy` (the fence post, with every roster gate) plus a two-mode fence structure. | Relabel it large, or accept that it may run long. | t10 |

### M1
`corridor_starts()` (`tests/helpers/specialist_exit_probe.gd:50-60`) heads each start away from its nearest edge, "exactly as the brains' `_enter_disengage()` do". The probe then enters DISENGAGE on a lone drone with no rig (`specialist_exit_probe.gd:170-178`). §2.12's Assault exit "along −n" has no frame there. The planet_approach density bound relies on the drone exit being ≲ 8.6 s, so this figure matters.

### M2
`PlayerBase._apply_damage` lets a `ShieldComponent` charge absorb a hit (`player_base.gd:128-141`). Charges come from `ShipProgressionState`, so the ±1 tolerance hides a missing hit.

### M3
The Phase 7 precedent (DECISIONS:2771) is a one-off headless measurement, not a GUT row.

### M4
`tasks.json` gives t6 `dependsOn: ["t1"]`. §2.7's `power_down()` cancels a TELEGRAPH beam or ring and fades an ACTIVE one, through `EnemyBeam` and `EnergyRing`, which come from t2 and t3. Adding t2 costs no wall-clock time, because t7 already waits on t5.

### M5
§2.10.1 asks for at least `coverage_min` 2 mounts in range. The heavy emplacement has two mounts with 700 px reach at the site origin.

### M6
Scope is closer to large. No re-split is needed.

Residual risk, not a finding: t1 must free at least 15 s of gate time after Phase 7 already took the easy levers (13.8 s). It may need a bit-identical production speed-up, or end with ESCALATE, and every other task waits on it. Full evidence is in `4-review.md`, round 2.
